verification_scope.variants: Read-only and tag operations cover powerpoint-visual-objects.pptx/.ppsx/.potx and powerpoint-passive-macro.pptm/.ppsm/.potm. These immutable native inputs do not contain the tested recommendation or tag owners; positive CRUD assertions apply to Litchi-authored derivatives.
verification_scope.raw_default_style: Pin all nine level indentation values (457200-EMU steps), 914400-EMU tab defaults, alignment and script line-breaking flags, nine 1800/1200 size/kerning values and +mn-lt theme fonts. An independent recommendation edit retains the entire presentation member and native discardImageEditData/defaultImageDpi/chartTrackingRefBased fragments. These are raw source/preservation checks, not typed Kinsoku/style semantics.
verification_scope.readonly: Absent, true and false are distinct. Create/update/remove, exact no-op, file reopen, forward replay, stale rejection and inverse retain all unrelated members. Recommendation removal retains the properties owner. A true recommendation permits a subsequent tag edit and does not become library access control.
verification_scope.tags: Direct slide and title-shape lists remain distinct and subtitle tags stay absent. Escaped Unicode literals and case-insensitive keys survive. Failed slide/shape selectors retain earlier staged work. Updates change only the respective tag part; removal collects the orphan part and preserves the other owner. Native shape content, title text and creation IDs are checked alongside exact unrelated payloads and graph-aware inverse checks.
verification_scope.laser: On native visual, macro and master-motion slide 1, store one three-point trace with 0/250/500-ms offsets and exact signed EMU coordinates. Replacement is the documented precise Invalid boundary; a refused second set preserves the first staged creation. File reopen, forward replay, stale rejection and inverse pass while native shape content/creation IDs and all other members remain exact.
verification_scope.events: The media and modern-media specimens both expose native video shape ID 4 on slide 2. Add seven typed trigger/play/pause/seek/resume/stop/null events targeting that object, with exact IDs/times/seek position, after adding a laser trace. Update to a null event at 800 ms, reject an empty event collection without losing staged work, and remove/invert after file reopen. The pre-existing laser and native creation IDs/common slide data/media payloads survive.
verification_scope.specification_check: Read-only research of the user-supplied [MS-PPTX] sections 2.3.3.16 (CT_MediaPlaybackEventRecord) and 2.3.3.17 (CT_MediaSeekEventRecord) confirms objId names a media object. Positive event tests therefore use the actual native video owner rather than a title-shape identifier. There is no runtime or test dependency on the research checkout.
verification_scope.ingress_and_graphs: Reader ingress retains the original ZIP for unchanged publication. Borrowed-buffer ingress can re-encode the ZIP but is separately checked for byte-exact member payloads. Graph-changing comparisons require identical member sets, complete relationship attributes and effective content types; all other payloads are exact. The new tag anchor correctly changes cSld, while its native spTree and creation ID remain exact.
verification_scope.limits: No native-authored recommendation/tag/laser/event evidence is claimed for these additions. Dedicated typed presentation default-style/Kinsoku access, line breaking, generic customer-data/schema semantics, arbitrary shared-anchor cases, laser replacement, event execution, rendering and fresh PowerPoint reopen remain outside the demonstrated scope. No macro or media execution occurred.
